content.text:
If you mean **free SiriusXM/satellite radio**, your legal options are limited:

- **SiriusXM Free Trial**: SiriusXM currently advertises free trials, including **3 months for $0** for some app-only plans and qualifying inactive radios. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/free-trial/?utm_source=openai))  
- **SiriusXM Free Access Plan**: Some eligible vehicles can get a limited set of **ad-supported channels for free**, but it depends on the vehicle/radio and does **not** include the mobile app. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/plans/free-access?utm_source=openai))  
- **Free Listen Events**: SiriusXM occasionally turns on inactive car radios for short promotional windows, but those are temporary.
- **NOAA Weather Radio**: If you mean free radio from government/weather sources, **NOAA Weather Radio** is free and broadcasts 24/7, but it’s weather/emergency info—not music or entertainment. ([weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/hnx/wxradio?utm_source=openai))  

There isn’t really a legal “free full satellite radio” service like SiriusXM without a trial, promo, or eligible free-access plan. Avoid “free satellite radio hacks” or pirate receivers—they’re illegal and often scams.
